subject: Normal change point model and test

messages.author: 31dc03607958a62a
messages.subject: Normal change point model and test
parts:
Hi users,

 y is form normal distribution with mean 0, standard deviation 1. Its length is 100. 
So I use the normal change model to detect a switching s in distribution. 
Then I determine s. But if I test mu1 (mean part before s) and mu2 (mean part after s), I find the probability (mu_diff<=0) is near 0.5.
Otherwise the histograms of Rhat and samples of mu_diff are below.

Could I say the switching s is false ? Or what could I conclude ?

Normal_CPM = "
data { 
  int<lower=1> N; #
  real y[N];
} 

transformed data{
  real log_unif;
  log_unif = -log(N);
}

parameters {
  vector[2] mu;
  real<lower=0> sigma;
} 

transformed parameters {
  vector[N] lp;
  vector[N+1] lp_e;
  vector[N+1] lp_l;
  lp_e[1] = 0;
  lp_l[1] = 0;
  for (t in 1:N) {
    lp_e[t + 1] = lp_e[t] + normal_lpdf(y[t] | mu[1], sigma);
    lp_l[t + 1] = lp_l[t] + normal_lpdf(y[t] | mu[2], sigma);
  }
  lp = rep_vector(log_unif + lp_l[N + 1], N) + head(lp_e, N) - head(lp_l, N);
}

model {
// Prior Distribution for Mean
  for(i in 1:2){
    mu[i] ~ normal(0,5);
  }
  sigma ~ normal(0,2);

// Observed Counts
  target += log_sum_exp(lp);
}

generated quantities {
  int<lower=1,upper=N> s;
  real mu_diff;
  s = categorical_rng(softmax(lp));
  mu_diff = mu[1] - mu[2];
}
"
# Generate data
y = rnorm(100)
N = length(y)

data_list = list(N=N, y=y)

# Compiling and producing posterior samples from the model.
stan_samples = stan(model_code = Normal_CPM, 
                    data = data_list,iter=5000, 
                    control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99))

# Results
posterior = as.data.frame(stan_samples)

stan_rhat(stan_samples)

hist(posterior$mu_diff)

mean(posterior$mu_diff <= 0)



Kind regards.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Normal change point model and test
parts:
There's an example of how to code a change-point model in the
manual chapter on latent discrete parameters. You'll see that
you need a slightly more involved loop than you have.

- Bob
